elements.element: Customer may assign to an affiliate without consent.
elements.evidence: Rendered § 22.4 permits consent-free assignment only "to a successor in connection with a merger, corporate reorganization or sale of all or substantially all of its assets, stock or securities"; no affiliate carve-out appears anywhere in the operative text, so an intra-group transfer to an Affiliate still needs M&I's consent.

elements.element: Customer may assign to a successor in a merger, acquisition, or sale of substantially all assets without consent.
elements.evidence: "either party may assign this Agreement without such consent, upon written notice to the other party, to a successor in connection with a merger, corporate reorganization or sale of all or substantially all of its assets, stock or securities" — Customer's former size/§ 21.11 conditions are removed.

elements.element: Vendor may not assign without Customer's consent.
elements.evidence: The rewritten proviso is mutual: M&I too "may assign this Agreement without such consent" to a merger/reorganization/asset-sale successor. To reach the preferred level the carve-out must be limited to Customer, leaving M&I subject to the consent requirement for all assignments.

elements.element: Customer's consent to Vendor assignment is not to be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: Retained opening words: "without the prior written consent of the other party, which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld".

elements.element: Vendor may never assign to a Customer competitor.
elements.evidence: No competitor prohibition appears in the rendered § 22.4 or in § 21.11(B); nothing bars M&I from assigning to a competitor of Customer.

elements.element: Customer's change of control gives Vendor no termination right.
elements.evidence: § 21.11(B) as retained obliges M&I to "continue to provide Services" on a Customer Change in Control, subject only to volume/entity scope limits; no termination or re-pricing right is conferred. (§ 11.3 is REDACTED and cannot be assessed, but nothing in the reviewable text grants a termination right.)

elements.element: Both parties may assign to a successor.
elements.evidence: "either party may assign this Agreement without such consent ... to a successor in connection with a merger, corporate reorganization or sale of all or substantially all of its assets, stock or securities" — symmetric on its face, replacing the former one-sided M&I free-assignment right and the size-conditioned Customer carve-out.

elements.element: A successor assignment requires written notice.
elements.evidence: "without such consent, upon written notice to the other party" — the notice condition attaches to the successor carve-out for both parties, curing M&I's former no-notice free assignment.

Retained: "This Agreement may not be assigned by either party, by operation of law or otherwise, without the prior written consent of the other party", with the carve-out limited to successor transactions.

elements.element: Consent to other assignments is not to be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: Retained: "which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld".

reasons: The fallback checklist is complete on the operative language: § 22.4 now gives both parties a successor-assignment right exercisable on written notice, and the pre-existing consent / not-unreasonably-withheld standard is retained verbatim for all other assignments. Position-complete at the fallback level.

Preferred level is not reached: there is no affiliate carve-out for Customer, no competitor prohibition on M&I, and the successor carve-out is mutual rather than Customer-only (M&I can still assign to a merger/asset-sale successor without our consent). To reach preferred, the drafter would need to (i) add "to an Affiliate of Customer or" to Customer's carve-out, (ii) confine the consent-free carve-out to Customer, and (iii) add "and in no event to a competitor of Customer" to M&I's assignment restriction.

Minimality holds. The edit is confined to the two asymmetric provisos that caused the fallback failure: former (a) (Customer's merger carve-out conditioned on a $100,000,000 capital-and-surplus acquirer and § 21.11 compliance) and former (b) (M&I's free assignment, including to a successor of the M&I Data Services division, with no notice). Both had to be rewritten to produce a mutual successor right on written notice; nothing outside the checklist was added — no survival tail, no expense or procedure language, no new remedies.

Intent preserved. The consent gate and reasonableness standard survive unchanged, § 21.11(B)'s Change-in-Control service-continuation and volume limits are untouched, and § 21.11 remains independently operative so deleting the "so long as the provisions of Section 21.11 are complied with" condition leaves no dangling cross-reference or undefined term. No retained sentence now contradicts the rewritten proviso.

Severity moderated: the walk-away triggers are absent (Customer is not blanket-prohibited from assigning, and no Vendor termination or re-pricing right arises on our Change in Control), so the defect was asymmetry and absence of notice rather than a walk-away term. The redacted § 11.3 reservation is correctly kept in the comment and not treated as an element.
